## Bugs found and fixed (one per module)

| Module | Bug | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| [wrap.py](file:textkit/wrap.py) | `< width` dropped words that fit exactly; also appended an empty line for empty input | `len(cur) + 1 + len(w) <= width`; only append non-empty `cur` |
| [slug.py](file:textkit/slug.py) | Replaced each punctuation char individually → `hello--world-`, no trimming | Collapse runs (`[^a-z0-9]+` → `-`) and strip leading/trailing hyphens |
| [roman.py](file:textkit/roman.py) | No subtractive pairs (`1994` → `MDCCCCLXXXXIIII`); `from_roman` added all values, so `IV` = 6; no range check | VALUES table with CM/CD/XC/XL/IX/IV; parser subtracts when a smaller numeral precedes a larger one; `ValueError` outside 1–3999 |
| [stats.py](file:textkit/stats.py) | Case-sensitive counting (`B` ≠ `b`), counted punctuation as part of words, no alphabetical tie-break | Lowercase, strip `string.punctuation`, sort by `(-count, word)` |
| [table.py](file:textkit/table.py) | Column widths taken from row 0 only; crashed on empty input | Widths = max over all rows (handles ragged rows); `render([])` → `""` |
| [dates.py](file:textkit/dates.py) | Slash format parsed as `%d/%m/%Y` (EU) → `10/02/2026` gave Feb 10 | `%m/%d/%Y` (US month/day/year) |

One judgment call: the original `test_table` expects no trailing space after the last column, so `render` right-strips each line; I noted that in the docstring.

Done — all six modules fixed, and the suite grew from 6 to 62 passing tests.

## Bugs found and fixed

| Module | Bug | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| [wrap.py](textkit/wrap.py) | `< width` instead of `<= width` broke lines at exactly `width`; a word ≥ width pushed a spurious empty first line; empty input returned `[""]` | Correct greedy fit (`len(cur) + 1 + len(w) <= width`), no empty lines, empty input → `[]` |
| [slug.py](textkit/slug.py) | Each punctuation char became its own hyphen (`hello--world-`) | Runs of non-alphanumerics (incl. underscores) collapse to one hyphen; leading/trailing hyphens stripped |
| [roman.py](textkit/roman.py) | No subtractive pairs (`1994` → `MDCCCCLXXXXIIII`); `from_roman` just added values; no error for n < 1 | Subtractive VALUES table; `from_roman` subtracts when a smaller symbol precedes a larger one; `ValueError` for n < 1 and for empty/unknown characters |
| [stats.py](textkit/stats.py) | Case-sensitive; no alphabetical tie-break; punctuation counted into words | Lowercase + tokenize on `[a-z0-9']+` (apostrophes kept, so `it's` stays one word); sort by `(-count, word)` |
| [table.py](textkit/table.py) | Widths taken from the first row only; crashed on empty input; trailing padding left on lines | Widths = max over all rows (ragged rows handled), `render([]) == ""`, lines rstripped |
| [dates.py](textkit/dates.py) | Slash format parsed as day/month/year | `%m/%d/%Y` (US); clearer `ValueError` message |

## Tests added ([tests/test_textkit.py](tests/test_textkit.py))

Every case you listed, plus a few natural extras:
- **wrap**: line of exactly `width` chars, word longer than width on its own line, empty/whitespace input, single word exactly `width`, and a sweep asserting no line exceeds `width` (except a lone long word)
- **slug**: repeated punctuation (`!!!`), leading/trailing punctuation and quotes, underscores, punctuation-only input → `""`
- **roman**: all six subtractive pairs in both directions, round-trip of 1–3999, `ValueError` for 0/negatives and for empty/unknown characters
- **word_freq**: case-insensitivity, punctuation ignored, alphabetical tie-break, empty/punctuation-only input, `top` larger than distinct words
- **table**: widest cell in first/middle/last row, no trailing padding, empty table, single row
- **dates**: all three formats with unambiguous values (`12/25/2026` proves US month-first), invalid formats raise `ValueError`

Two judgment calls worth noting: `from_roman` accepts additive forms like `IIII` and malformed-but-parseable ones like `IC` (the docstring promises ValueError only for empty/unknown characters — strict validation would be a different contract), and `word_freq` keeps apostrophes inside words. Both are covered by tests. Final run: **62 passed**, plus a manual spot-check of leap-day parsing, ragged tables, and error messages.
